target.title: RFC 0017: Command Catalog
target.body:
## Why this exists

Compliance and enterprise operations need a dependable answer to a basic question: **what command surfaces can this OpenClaw deployment expose?** Today that information is spread across core CLI descriptors, routed commands, the live Commander tree, plugins, and paired nodes.

A shared, read-only inventory would let operators and automation enumerate those surfaces and consistently report provenance, read versus mutation effects, confirmation requirements, and elevated risk where the owning registry knows them. It would not execute commands or become a policy engine.

Existing issues show demand for parts of this capability, though none is an exact duplicate:

- [#52919](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/52919): runtime command discovery for remote clients
- [#77943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77943): inconsistent machine-readable list output
- [#50011](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50011): node policy names that do not match known commands
- [#77730](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77730): configured plugin node commands diverging from runtime advertisement

Prompt-related requests provide evidence for one future consumer: [#14619](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/14619) covers duplicated tool-list prompt text, [#14785](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/14785) covers tool-schema token overhead, and [#41417](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41417) requests assembled-prompt inspection. The same inventory could later support generated docs, compatibility fixtures, diagnostics, policy checks, and scoped operator/model views. The initial CLI does not claim prompt-token savings.

## What this RFC proposes

A read-only **Command Catalog** built from command information OpenClaw already owns.

### Option A: commands list and inspect (recommended)

```text
openclaw commands list
openclaw commands inspect <command-path...>
```

This option follows noun-based groups such as `plugins` and `skills`, stays command-owned, and excludes ownerless tool adapters and aggregate audit/test/summary reports.

- [Upstream implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100960)
- [PR1: commands list](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/24)
- [PR2: commands inspect](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/25)
- [Optional PR3: scoped command prompt projection](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/26)

PR3 is a separately reviewed follow-up on the fork. It is not included in the initial upstream implementation.

### Option B: broader catalog

```text
openclaw catalog list
openclaw catalog audit
openclaw catalog test-matrix
openclaw catalog summary
```

This remains available as a concrete alternative with command-like tool adapters and operational lenses.

- [Catalog foundation](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/11)
- [Dynamic/operator lenses](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/12)

## Existing Gateway surface

Gateway `commands.list` remains the agent-facing chat/native/skill/plugin inventory. Option A adds an operator/developer CLI inventory; it does not replace or change that RPC. Future convergence is a maintainer decision.

## ClawSweeper follow-up completed

The linked implementation now:

- fails closed on plugin loader exceptions and error-level plugin diagnostics;
- emits no valid-looking JSON when a requested plugin scan is incomplete;
- documents `effectProfile`, `commandExposure`, and `hidden`, including defaults and an external-plugin example; and
- includes terminal proof for core-only, plugin-enabled, and controlled plugin-failure paths; and
- adds a discoverable `openclaw commands` CLI reference covering scope, options, output, and failure semantics.

Proof summary from `90a7b1ca2b`:

```text
core:    descriptors=61 runtime=26 plugins=0
plugins: descriptors=61 runtime=26 plugins=3
failure: exit=1 stdoutBytes=0 expectedError=true
```

## Lifecycle boundary

The RFC remains `draft`. The required OpenClaw `maintainer-discussion` thread still must be created and linked before acceptance. Namespace, stable schema, plugin metadata, and Gateway convergence are maintainer decisions rather than contributor-declared contracts.

## Feedback requested

- Is the recommended `openclaw commands` boundary clear and useful?
- How should it eventually relate to Gateway `commands.list` and live paired-node command declarations?
- Which JSON fields should be stable beyond schema version, identity, and provenance?

target.title: RFC 0018: Readiness Conditions and Providers
target.body:
## Decision requested

Should OpenClaw modernize its existing fixed Gateway readiness evaluator into one structured, extensible condition contract?

This RFC covers **readiness conditions and providers only**. Standard Hosting Profiles have moved to a separate RFC so the readiness facility can be accepted and used independently.

## Implementer specification

The normative V1 contract is the [Readiness v1 specification](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/rfcs/blob/user/giodl/standard-hosting-profiles-ready-check/rfcs/0018/readiness-v1-spec.md). The RFC carries the design rationale and rollout plan; the sidecar is the schema, provider lifecycle, bounded evaluation, projection, and conformance reference.

## Problem

OpenClaw already exposes `/ready` and `/readyz`, but the evaluator is purpose-built around a fixed set of Gateway observations. Today:

- startup, drain, channel, and event-loop observations do not share one iterable condition shape;
- plugins cannot contribute bounded readiness observations;
- operators cannot explicitly require a known plugin-owned dependency;
- health and status may omit or represent readiness facts differently; and
- hosts add private scripts for missing facts such as workspace writability.

The result is ambiguity between "the process responds" and "this runtime can accept work."

## Proposed v1

Every observation uses one stable shape:

```text
type + status + requirement + reason + message
```

- Required `False` or `Unknown` conditions fail readiness.
- Advisory conditions remain visible without causing an outage.
- Existing Gateway startup, drain, channel, and event-loop observations become canonical core conditions.
- Existing `failing`, `suppressed`, and `eventLoop` fields remain compatibility projections.
- `/ready`, `/readyz`, health, status, and an optional CLI project the same result.
- `/healthz` remains shallow liveness.

## Direct use without profiles

The RFC is directly useful on its own. Universal Gateway lifecycle conditions always apply; an operator may explicitly add registered core or plugin criteria as required or advisory:

```json5
{
  gateway: {
    readiness: {
      requiredCriteria: [
        "openclaw.workspace-writable",
        "plugin.storage.backend",
      ],
      advisoryCriteria: ["plugin.metrics.exporter"],
    },
  },
}
```

Registering a criterion does not make it a blocker. Existing installations do not acquire new required workspace or plugin dependencies. Only explicit operator configuration, or a separately selected hosting profile, adds requirements beyond the universal baseline.

## Plugin providers

Only activated plugins may register executable providers through `OpenClawPluginApi`. Operators reference IDs; they cannot inject callbacks through config.

Providers are:

- activation-scoped and atomically replaced on reload;
- namespaced and enumerable without exposing callbacks;
- observational, read-only, and idempotent;
- advisory by default;
- bounded by per-provider deadlines and an outer watchdog; and
- converted to stable `Unknown` results on timeout or error.

Core retains ownership of invocation, cancellation, coalescing, caching, validation, redaction, and result ordering. If a callback ignores cancellation after its deadline, later polls reuse the stable timeout result and do not start duplicate work. If the canonical evaluator itself times out or fails, every projection receives a redacted required `ReadinessEvaluationComplete=Unknown` condition rather than a rejected health/status request.

## Compatibility and boundaries

This proposal extends existing Gateway readiness. It does not add a second health service, policy engine, OCC dependency, hosting abstraction, or config system.

It does not define profile names, profile selection, activation identity, or release profile conformance. Those product/support decisions are isolated in the Standard Hosting Profiles RFC.

Readiness also remains distinct from state continuity: `/ready` says whether this runtime can serve work now; it does not prove checkpoint durability or safe destruction.

## Primary implementation

The primary implementation to review is [openclaw/openclaw#104018](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104018). It is the proposed upstream landing shape: one implementation PR with four ordered commits at exact head `17b34f792d8`, rebased onto OpenClaw `main` at `4e78d91c0f9`, with exact-head tests, published-upgrade evidence, and package-installed Docker proof.

The fork PRs below expose those same commits as optional smaller review slices. They are supporting review aids, not alternative landing PRs:

| Slice | Draft PR | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical core conditions | [PR 17](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/17) | Normalize existing Gateway observations and compatibility projections. |
| Workspace readiness | [PR 22](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/22) | Add one bounded core criterion without profile behavior. |
| Readiness providers and explicit requirements | [PR 23](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/23) | Add plugin registration and direct `gateway.readiness` selection. |
| Canonical readiness CLI | [PR 27](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/27) | Add `openclaw ready` as a thin projection of the live result. |

The [consolidated implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104018) contains the same four review slices. Its exact package proves `/ready` and `/readyz` transition `200 -> 503 -> 200`, `/healthz` remains live, and `openclaw ready --json` exits `0 -> 1 -> 0` with the same canonical condition. A published `2026.7.1 -> 2026.7.2` upgrade lane also proves existing installations retain their readiness baseline instead of silently acquiring opt-in criteria.

## Maintainer questions

1. Is the required/advisory condition model the right modernization of the existing evaluator?
2. Is activation-scoped plugin registration the right extension boundary?
3. Is explicit `gateway.readiness` selection sufficient for v1 without profiles?

Profile naming, profile support ownership, runtime activation identity, and release conformance can now be reviewed independently.
